# The dependency closure of `mixengine-elevate` built on its own, as `lint` regenerates and diffs it.
# Everything here runs as root. Adding a line is a security decision — see D8 of
# docs/specs/2026-08-22-t40-elevate-design.md, and the comment above `[dependencies]` in
# crates/mixengine-elevate/Cargo.toml.
# Generated on Linux, which is where the `lint` job runs:
#   cargo tree -p mixengine-elevate --no-default-features --edges normal --prefix none --format '{p}' | sed 's/ v[0-9].*//' | sort -u
#
# The system trust store added two: `pem` and its `base64`. The helper writes MixEngine's authority
# into an anchors directory on Linux and hands it to `security` on macOS, and both of those are PEM
# text; Windows carries DER through its certificate-store API and never sees an envelope, so the
# dependency is declared under `cfg(unix)`. Two crates, measured against the 22 `x509-parser` would
# have cost and the 8 `sha2` would — both of which the trust-store work refused, writing its own
# DER reader instead. What these buy is base64 padding rules nobody should hand-write, at the
# version `rcgen` pins so the workspace holds one copy. See D11 of
# docs/specs/2026-08-24-t49a-system-trust-store-design.md.
#
# The helper's update added one: `minisign-verify`, and it brings nothing with it — the crate has no
# dependencies of its own and vendors the Ed25519 and Blake2b it needs. It is what checks a
# replacement helper inside the elevated process, against a key compiled into the copy already
# installed, which is the single rule `docs/features/updates.md` calls the most important on its
# page. Weighed against the eight crates `sha2` would have cost, which is the trade the trust store
# refused two paragraphs up.
base64
itoa
libc
memchr
minisign-verify
mixengine-elevate
mixengine-platform
mixengine-proto
pem
proc-macro2
quote
serde
